title: Mathematical properties of 24 and the vision of Zechariah
english: Standing by, he who says these things says that the Almighty will do such things; for having great compassion and extreme goodness, he calls those who distance themselves from God and from virtue to return and draw near, so that having approached him and staying near him, they may obtain eternal salvation, according to what is written: 'Draw near to the Lord and he will draw near to you' (James 4:8). These said retreats and proximities occur in relation and disposition, but not in place.

Turning to me, and I to you. You do not become like those who begot you according to wickedness, whom the prophets called before the present time, so that you might not suffer the same things as them. And what did they call to them? Or to turn away from faulty customs and evil ways? But not having heard and not having attended to them, they perished along with those deceived by false prophets, so that there are no longer even the foxes or those snatched away by their sorcery. Since therefore neither the prophets nor the deceived are [present], you, to whom I bring the word of God, walk the divine ways and do not pursue the evil ones.

For divine and profitable instructions are announced to us in our Spirit—this is the Holy—by my servants the prophets who have it; for these, having the Spirit of truth and being prepared by it for speaking, benefit those who pay attention to them, of whom those called fathers have had experience; because they neither heard nor paid attention to them, they were answered through their works. Just as the Lord has stretched out to do, so it shall happen to them, even if God has stirred them to repentance, so that they might not suffer the things threatened.

In the fourth and sixth [month] in the twelfth month—this is the month of Sabbath—in the second year of Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying (Zechariah 1:7). All things happening and being given by God have order and harmony which has proportion, 'doing great and unsearchable things,' 'arranging all by measure and number.' Moreover, the word of the prophet lying before us, becoming visible more by scientific theory than by being heard, is arranged having much certainty according to number in a tetrad...

And the twenty-fourth of the twelfth month according to the Hebrews. The number 24 is powerful as a square; for this is divided by its parts thus: half 12, a third 8, a fourth 6, a sixth 4, an eighth 3, a twelfth 2, a twenty-fourth 1. That which is born from 24 according to the composition of its parts is a square, for six times six. And nothing is so certain of forms as the square.

The one before us has an exceptional quality, that each of its sides has composed a perfect number, the six. Likewise with 24, and the 12, being composed of its parts, produces a square: half 6, a third 4, a fourth 3, a sixth 2, a twelfth 1; these parts, being composed together, fulfill the sixteen, the latter being also a square, a small square of four. And this has an exceptional quality according to its own sides; for the square is a ten in power thus: 1, 2, 3, 4.

I saw in the night, and behold a man riding a red horse, and he was standing among the two mountains of shade, and behind him red and mixed and variegated and white horses (Zechariah 1:8). When the word of the Lord came to Zechariah by night, there was seen to him a man riding a red horse, standing among the two mountains of shade (Zechariah 1:7). And the man riding the red horse is the Savior who became man. And a red horse is that which surrounds a body; for the human flesh is red by nature, because blood flows through it. But where did he see the man standing, and between whom, and when was the one receiving God to stand watch?

He saw him, then, 'among the mountains of shade.' These two covenants happen to be fruitful and shady because of the density of meanings and the ambiguity of the words concerning theology and incarnation. And since each of those announced in the two covenants has much obscurity with enigma and depth, in a night he saw the approach of the man to the horse, similarly to what was said about him: 'He set darkness as his hidden garment' (Zechariah 6:5); for in this expression, that which is hidden is signified by the obscurity, just as in: 'The abyss was as his enveloping garment' (Psalm 183:6). title: Isaiah's multifaceted ministry and the indwelling Christ
english: It has been viewed theologically. And those following him come behind him; for Moses, the great theophany, not yet being able to see his face knowningly, has been set to see those behind him, that is, those with him, and not other things existing of the creation of God. For having neglected to show those after God, which are called behind him, he wrote down the Creation, beginning from: 'In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth' (Gen 1:1).

A different color of the horses behind the one appearing is written down, since some of them are men, and others are divine 'spirits, being sent for service for those about to inherit salvation.' For those who have handed over the human things of the Word's appearing and becoming flesh, are red, especially since even he, behind whom they exist, says 'a garment of red from Bozrah,' as it was said to him by those who saw: 'Why are your garments red?' saying his garments which surround the flesh and the blood sprinkled upon it. These things have been made more clear in the commentaries of the prophet Isaiah.

After the red horses behind the one being praised, various and dappled and white horses appeared. And perhaps the various and dappled ones are those who lead the teaching in many ways concerning the sensible and the intelligible, which the divine words say are 'visible and invisible,' while the white ones are those announcing the theological things apart from all matter. It must be said according to another thought that the various and dappled ones are those fitting in teaching to the various condition of those being instructed. Or was not Paul a various horse, being a follower of the Christ speaking in him, when to the Jews he became a Jew to win these, and to the lawless as lawless, to turn them from the lawless disposition, and to those under law as under law, so that he might win them also, persuading them to transcend 'the law of shadow' (Heb 10:1)? After having said these things, he says: 'I have become all things to all, so that I might save all' (1 Cor 9:22).

And not only those after the appearing, but also those before it had this variety, participating in 'the manifold wisdom of God' (Eph 3:10), of which it is enough to mention two, so that the discourse may not become long, d...

Having been present and having moved to the others by thought. 1.28 Isaiah, having received all the kinds of helpful words from God through divine visions, possessed them all at once. For as a prophet, seeing the things that were to come with a prophetic eye (Isa 7:14), he said: 'Behold, the virgin shall conceive in her womb, and shall bear a son.' As a lawgiver, he commanded and forbade, saying: 'Cease from your evils, learn to do good' (Isa 1:16). But he also wrote history concerning King Sennacherib of the Assyrians and Hezekiah, who held sway over the Hebrews. Along with these was song, where he says: 'I will sing indeed to the beloved a song of the beloved to my vineyard' (Isa 12:5), and where: 'On that day they shall sing this new song: Behold, a strong city, and our salvation' (Isa 25:1).

1.29 Likewise David, as a singer, said: 'O God, a new song we will sing to you'; as a lawgiver: 'Turn away from evil and do good' (Ps 17:14); as one foretelling the future, he cried out: 'The God of gods shall be seen in Zion' (Ps 50:5). Nor did the historical narrative fail, having detailed many things that happened sensuously against the Egyptians and Pharaoh for the sake of the Israelites in many psalms. 1.30 What then are the spiritual horses that worked behind the man mounted on a red horse? In the following words of the prophet at hand, let us see.

1.31 Zach. I, 9: 'And I said, What are these, Lord? And the angel speaking in me said to me, I will show you what these are.' 1.32 The prophet himself says to the angel speaking in him: 'What are these, Lord?' And the angel speaking in him—that is, the angel standing by the prophecy—is he, or according to another thought, is it the Savior himself, about whom the prophet says: 'His name shall be called Angel of Great Counsel' (Isa 9:6). And the teacher speaks in the listener when he participates in him or is by disposition in him.

1.33 The testimony of the former is: 'But Christ lives in me,' and also: 'Of the Christ speaking in me.' By this understanding also the singer said: 'I will listen to what the Lord God will speak in me,' and Habakkuk: 'I will stand watching to see what the Lord will speak in me' (Hab 2:1). title: The Rest of the Dwelling and the Virgin Bride
english: While learning according to intellect and the quality of the lessons. For they are doing only this thing, making a buzzing noise in the ear, not benefiting the understanding of those being instructed; and what one speaks and speaks to him, is not always the one striking the ear in the heart speaking.

And the man who stood in the midst of the mountains answered and said to me: 'These are those whom the Lord has sent to go around the earth' (Zechariah 1:10). If anyone were to seek what comes from where, having seen the prophet's coming horses, red, varied, speckled, white, the speaking angel promises him to show him what was seen.

Not then, since there is a twofold vision concerning these, one more introductory and one having ascended higher, to the one who has known the introductory showing, the divine instructor promises the more perfect one, having received the perfect love of the revelation. The man who stood in the midst of the mentioned mountains answered twice: 'These are those whom the Lord has sent to go around the earth' (Zechariah 1:10).

According to a second vision, the people from the Hebrews and the nations happen to be overshadowed by two mountains, of whom, standing in the midst, the man already interpreted initiates into the mystery who those sent to go around the earth are. And they are excellent teachers from among men and angels, as it has been said nearby.

It is not in vain that they were sent to go around the earth by the Lord, not all of those promising to teach or those going around having been sent by the Lord. 'Going indeed around the earth' is the devil, as he himself said, in the examining of Job and the other athletes of God, doing this by especially bad intention, but not having been handed over by God.

What then do the sent ones say they have seen in the going around, or that the whole earth is inhabited and is at rest, as the following wording presents it thus. And they answered the angel of the Lord who stood in the midst of the mountains, and they said: 'We have gone around all the earth and behold, all the earth is inhabited and is at rest' (Zechariah 1:11).

Since not every angel is of the Lord, it is not even of him those having left the heavenly dwelling, so it is fitting that the ones going around answer the angel of the Lord as if the whole earth is being inhabited.

And it rests. Regarding the apostates, even if they are simply called angels, they do not serve the Lord, which is still clearly shown from the scriptures, where it says: 'God did not spare angels who sinned' (Hebrews 11:34 / 2 Peter 2:4), for he did not say that; but where it is said by the Apostle speaking in Christ: 'We shall judge angels' (Jude 1:6 / 2 Peter 2:4).

One should consider what it means for the whole earth to dwell and to be at rest. Since the rational soul is self-moving and ever-moving, when it moves well and blessedly, it is calm and rests from disordered shaking, and it bears this stability from divine reverence.

For it is written: 'The earth was afraid and was still when God arose to judgment' (Psalm 46:2), and: 'He who dwells on hope is still from every evil' (Proverbs 1:33), according to the inspired writing of the Proverbs. By this understanding, regarding the agitator Cain, moved as if God says: 'You sinned, be still' (Genesis 4:7), he is not only saying: 'Having sinned with disordered shaking, put an end to the disordered impulse'; for then you will be praised to be still, 'turning away from evil and doing good' (Proverbs 4:27).

To him who thus rests, dwelling follows. As for how this is, the prostitute woman introduced in Proverbs—whoever this is—'does not have feet that rest in the house' (Proverbs 7:11), having them wandering outside, being a wayward and serious woman, dwelling in the house of a noblewoman and a lady, guarding the lawful marriage rites toward the bridegroom, which is immediately followed by bearing children. For it is said in the Psalms concerning the bride of God the Word: 'He who dwells in the house, having once been a virgin, so that he may become a mother of legitimate children, rejoicing' (Psalm 45:4).
The angel of the Lord answered and said: 'Lord Almighty, how long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, which you overlook, until this seventieth year?' (Zechariah 1:12).

Having seen prophetically the angel of the Lord Almighty the whole earth dwelling and resting, and all the nations having believed in the Lord who came among them, he deems it worthy to be granted the knowledge of the King of all, until when and when Jerusalem and the cities of Judah beneath it will be shown mercy, the seventieth year of the captivity already having entered, through which they seemed to be passing by.
